purpose: Capture user-supplied column molding and compound-pier references as measured source profiles before generating finished assets.

references.observed_subject: Measured classical column/pedestal side profiles with cap, fluted shaft, base, plinth, and centimeter callouts.
Compound pier diagram showing arch, pier, shaft, and lobed cross-section.

shape_controls.dominant_silhouette: wide flat cap over concave-convex side curve and narrow necking bands
shape_controls.intended_profile_points: trace as a small ordered custom_polygon in local xz, then revolve or extrude by asset family
shape_controls.curve_handling: use low point count first, then bevel or shade for apparent roundness

candidate_blender_tools.use: Create the traced side-profile polygon deterministically.
Revolve the side profile when building a column cap.
Round the narrow lip and bead edges without adding source-side complexity.
Improve hard-surface shading after bevels.

implementation_notes: This is the first cap profile source; it is not yet a generated column asset.
The visible centimeter callouts are recorded as source hints, not production dimensions.

shape_controls.dominant_silhouette: repeated shallow rounded flutes around or across a shaft face
shape_controls.intended_profile_points: define one channel as a low-vertex concave custom polygon, then repeat by array
shape_controls.curve_handling: represent the flute with a small faceted arc and let bevel/normal tools sell the carved edge

candidate_blender_tools.use: Build one simple fluted channel profile.
Repeat channels across a rectangular shaft side.
Repeat channel cutters or raised ribs around a shaft.
Round the flute lips while keeping the channel source low vertex.

implementation_notes: This profile is the bridge between the user's simple-vertex idea and visually complex ribbing.
The generator should expose channel count, depth, and lip width as controls.

shape_controls.dominant_silhouette: large round torus-like swelling over narrow stacked bands
shape_controls.intended_profile_points: trace the side silhouette as a faceted custom polygon and optionally revolve with screw
shape_controls.curve_handling: bevel and weighted normals should provide rounded stone without high source vertex count

candidate_blender_tools.use: Create the torus-side silhouette from declared profile points.
Revolve the base profile into a column base.
Add catch-light rounding to bands and torus edges.
Smooth the visually round swelling after profile generation.

implementation_notes: This should replace generic square base slabs when a column source calls for a classical base.
The 8 cm callout is treated as visual proportion evidence, not a fabrication radius.

shape_controls.dominant_silhouette: stepped plinth with an ogee-like rounded transition into a broad foot
shape_controls.intended_profile_points: use a stepped custom polygon with a small number of curve control corners
shape_controls.curve_handling: the source stores the important silhouette breaks; bevels can create the soft stone transitions

candidate_blender_tools.use: Build a traced plinth profile with explicit silhouette corners.
Add broad square plinth slabs when the profile is used in a blocky post.
Round selected profile edges after extrusion or screw revolve.
Keep major plinth steps crisp after beveling.

implementation_notes: This is the profile most likely to improve square-to-round base transitions in the next column/post recipe.
The shape is intentionally stored as source morphology, not Blender-specific modeling steps.

shape_controls.dominant_silhouette: central compound shaft with four major lobes, smaller intermediate lobes, and vertical clustered ribs
shape_controls.intended_profile_points: declare a lobed custom_polygon or generate lobes from normalized radii before extrusion
shape_controls.curve_handling: start with faceted lobes; later add bevels or radial duplicated half-round ribs

candidate_blender_tools.use: Create the lobed cross-section as a deterministic low-vertex mesh profile.
Add simple shaft lobes or column clusters when the source chooses separate solids.
Repeat rib/lobe members around the central pier.
Join compound pier members after source-defined placement.
Soften rib edges while preserving the lobed silhouette.

implementation_notes: This establishes the compound-pier cross-section as reusable source data for posts, columns, frame mullions, and pier-like supports.
The numbers are normalized because the reference diagram is a form diagram, not a measured construction drawing.

next_generation_goal.first_geometry_change: Compile one square plinth, cap/base molding, fluted shaft, and compound-lobed cross-section into a Blender tool plan.
